**George E. Pataki** (b. June 24, 1945, in Peekskill, [N.Y.](https://ballotpedia.org/New_York "New York")) is a former [Republican](https://ballotpedia.org/Republican "Republican")[governor of New York](https://ballotpedia.org/Governor_of_New_York "Governor of New York"), serving three terms from 1995 to 2007.[[1]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-bio-1) On May 28, 2015, Pataki announced he was running for [president of the United States](https://ballotpedia.org/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") in 2016.[[2]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-announce-2) He suspended his presidential campaign on December 29, 2015.[[3]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-3)

## Biography

Email [editor@ballotpedia.org](mailto:editor@ballotpedia.org?subject=Bio%20update%20for%20George%20Pataki) to notify us of updates to this biography. 

Pataki was raised on a farm in Peekskill, N.Y. He attended Yale University on a scholarship and actively participated in politics on campus, including serving as the chairman of the college's Conservative Party. After graduating from Yale in 1967, Pataki attended Columbia Law School where he received his law degree in 1970.[[4]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-yale-4)

Pataki first entered office a decade later when he became [mayor](https://ballotpedia.org/Mayor "Mayor") of Peekskill in 1981. He was then elected to the [New York State Assembly](https://ballotpedia.org/New_York_State_Assembly "New York State Assembly") in 1984, and he served in that role until 1993, when he became a [state senator](https://ballotpedia.org/New_York_State_Senate "New York State Senate"). Pataki defeated Mario Cuomo in 1994 to become the first [Republican](https://ballotpedia.org/Republican "Republican") governor of New York in 20 years. He remained in that role for three terms from 1995 to 2007.[[5]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-5) Pataki's service as governor was defined by his leadership during the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.[[6]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-6)

After leaving office, Pataki joined Chadbourne & Parke LLP as counsel on environmental and corporate matters.[[7]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-7) Pataki also founded a business development firm with [John Cahill](https://ballotpedia.org/John_Cahill "John Cahill"), the Pataki-Cahill Group.[[8]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-8)

## Presidential preference

In January 2016, Pataki endorsed [Marco Rubio](https://ballotpedia.org/Marco_Rubio "Marco Rubio") (R), but Rubio ended his campaign in February.[[9]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-9) In April 2016, ahead of the New York primary, Pataki endorsed [John Kasich](https://ballotpedia.org/John_Kasich "John Kasich") (R).

### 2016 presidential endorsement

## Political career

### New York Governor (1995 to 2007)

Pataki served as the [governor of New York](https://ballotpedia.org/Governor_of_New_York "Governor of New York") for three terms between 1995 and 2007.[[1]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-bio-1)

### New York State Senate (1993 to 1995)

Pataki served in the [New York State Senate](https://ballotpedia.org/New_York_State_Senate "New York State Senate") from 1993 to 1995. He left the state Senate in 1995 after being elected governor in November 1994.[[1]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-bio-1)

### New York State Assembly (1985 to 1993)

Pataki was first elected to the [New York State Assembly](https://ballotpedia.org/New_York_State_Assembly "New York State Assembly") in 1984. He served in that role until 1993, when he became a state senator.[[1]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-bio-1)

### Mayor of Peekskill (1981 to 1985)

Pataki served one term as [mayor](https://ballotpedia.org/Mayor "Mayor") of Peekskill from 1981 to 1985.[[4]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-yale-4)

**George E. Pataki** (b. June 24, 1945, in Peekskill, [N.Y.](https://ballotpedia.org/New_York "New York")) is a former [Republican](https://ballotpedia.org/Republican "Republican")[governor of New York](https://ballotpedia.org/Governor_of_New_York "Governor of New York"), serving three terms from 1995 to 2007.[[1]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-bio-1) On May 28, 2015, Pataki announced he was running for [president of the United States](https://ballotpedia.org/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") in 2016.[[2]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-announce-2) He suspended his presidential campaign on December 29, 2015.[[3]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-3)

## Biography

Email [editor@ballotpedia.org](mailto:editor@ballotpedia.org?subject=Bio%20update%20for%20George%20Pataki) to notify us of updates to this biography. 

Pataki was raised on a farm in Peekskill, N.Y. He attended Yale University on a scholarship and actively participated in politics on campus, including serving as the chairman of the college's Conservative Party. After graduating from Yale in 1967, Pataki attended Columbia Law School where he received his law degree in 1970.[[4]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-yale-4)

Pataki first entered office a decade later when he became [mayor](https://ballotpedia.org/Mayor "Mayor") of Peekskill in 1981. He was then elected to the [New York State Assembly](https://ballotpedia.org/New_York_State_Assembly "New York State Assembly") in 1984, and he served in that role until 1993, when he became a [state senator](https://ballotpedia.org/New_York_State_Senate "New York State Senate"). Pataki defeated Mario Cuomo in 1994 to become the first [Republican](https://ballotpedia.org/Republican "Republican") governor of New York in 20 years. He remained in that role for three terms from 1995 to 2007.[[5]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-5) Pataki's service as governor was defined by his leadership during the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.[[6]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-6)

After leaving office, Pataki joined Chadbourne & Parke LLP as counsel on environmental and corporate matters.[[7]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-7) Pataki also founded a business development firm with [John Cahill](https://ballotpedia.org/John_Cahill "John Cahill"), the Pataki-Cahill Group.[[8]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-8)

## Presidential preference

In January 2016, Pataki endorsed [Marco Rubio](https://ballotpedia.org/Marco_Rubio "Marco Rubio") (R), but Rubio ended his campaign in February.[[9]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-9) In April 2016, ahead of the New York primary, Pataki endorsed [John Kasich](https://ballotpedia.org/John_Kasich "John Kasich") (R).

### 2016 presidential endorsement

✓ Pataki endorsed [John Kasich](https://ballotpedia.org/John_Kasich_presidential_campaign,_2016 "John Kasich presidential campaign, 2016") for the Republican primary in the 2016 U.S. [presidential election](https://ballotpedia.org/Presidential_election,_2016 "Presidential election, 2016").[[10]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-10)

## Political career

### New York Governor (1995 to 2007)

Pataki served as the [governor of New York](https://ballotpedia.org/Governor_of_New_York "Governor of New York") for three terms between 1995 and 2007.[[1]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-bio-1)

### New York State Senate (1993 to 1995)

Pataki served in the [New York State Senate](https://ballotpedia.org/New_York_State_Senate "New York State Senate") from 1993 to 1995. He left the state Senate in 1995 after being elected governor in November 1994.[[1]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-bio-1)

### New York State Assembly (1985 to 1993)

Pataki was first elected to the [New York State Assembly](https://ballotpedia.org/New_York_State_Assembly "New York State Assembly") in 1984. He served in that role until 1993, when he became a state senator.[[1]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-bio-1)

### Mayor of Peekskill (1981 to 1985)

Pataki served one term as [mayor](https://ballotpedia.org/Mayor "Mayor") of Peekskill from 1981 to 1985.[[4]](https://ballotpedia.org/George_Pataki#cite_note-yale-4)

[Kathy Hochul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathy_Hochul "Kathy Hochul") has been governor since August 24, 2021. She is the first woman to hold the position. 

The [governor of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_New_York "Governor of New York") is the [head of government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_government "Head of government") of the [U.S. state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State "New York State"), the head of the [executive branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_(government) "Executive (government)") of [New York's state government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_New_York_(state) "Government of New York (state)"), and the [commander-in-chief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander-in-chief "Commander-in-chief") of the state's [military forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Division_of_Military_and_Naval_Affairs "New York State Division of Military and Naval Affairs").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-a4s3-1) The officeholder has a duty to enforce state laws, to convene the [New York State Legislature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Legislature "New York State Legislature"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-a4s3-1) the power to either approve or [veto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veto "Veto")[bills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_(law) "Bill (law)") passed by the legislature,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-2) as well as to grant [pardons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pardon "Pardon"), except in cases of [treason](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treason "Treason") and [impeachment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_in_the_United_States "Impeachment in the United States").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-3)

Fifty-seven people have served as state governor, four of whom served non-consecutive terms ([George Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Clinton_(vice_president) "George Clinton (vice president)"), [DeWitt Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeWitt_Clinton "DeWitt Clinton"), [Horatio Seymour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horatio_Seymour "Horatio Seymour"), and [Al Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Smith "Al Smith")); the official numbering lists each governor only once. There has only been one female governor so far: [Kathy Hochul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathy_Hochul "Kathy Hochul"). This numbering includes one acting governor: the lieutenant governor who filled the vacancy after the resignation of the governor, under the 1777 Constitution.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-4) The list does not include the prior colonial governors nor those who have acted as governor when the governor was out of state, such as Lieutenant Governor Timothy L. Woodruff during Theodore Roosevelt's vice presidential campaign in 1900, or Acting [Speaker of the New York State Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Speakers_of_the_New_York_State_Assembly "List of Speakers of the New York State Assembly")[Moses M. Weinstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_M._Weinstein "Moses M. Weinstein"), who acted as governor for 10 days in 1968 while the governor, the Lieutenant Governor and the Senate Majority Leader were out of the state, attending the Republican National Convention in [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami "Miami").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-5)

Four men have become [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") after serving as governor of New York: [Martin Van Buren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Van_Buren "Martin Van Buren"), [Grover Cleveland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grover_Cleveland "Grover Cleveland"), [Theodore Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Roosevelt "Theodore Roosevelt"), and [Franklin D. Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt "Franklin D. Roosevelt"), and six were [vice president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_president_of_the_United_States "Vice president of the United States"). Van Buren and Theodore Roosevelt held both offices. Numerous Governors have also sought the Presidency, and won their party's respective nomination, but lost the general election, such as [Al Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Smith "Al Smith"), [Samuel J. Tilden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_J._Tilden "Samuel J. Tilden"), [Horatio Seymour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horatio_Seymour "Horatio Seymour"), [Thomas E. Dewey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_E._Dewey "Thomas E. Dewey"), and [Charles Evans Hughes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Evans_Hughes "Charles Evans Hughes"). Two governors have been [chief justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Justice_of_the_United_States "Chief Justice of the United States"): [John Jay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Jay "John Jay") held that position when he was elected governor in 1795, and [Charles Evans Hughes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Evans_Hughes "Charles Evans Hughes") became chief justice in 1930, two decades after leaving the governorship.

The longest-serving governor was the first, [George Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Clinton_(vice_president) "George Clinton (vice president)"), who first took office on July 30, 1777, and served seven terms in two different periods, totaling just under 21 years in office. As 18 of those years were consecutive, Clinton also served the longest consecutive period in office for a New York governor. [Charles Poletti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Poletti "Charles Poletti") had the shortest term, serving 29 days following the resignation of the previous governor, [Herbert H. Lehman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_H._Lehman "Herbert H. Lehman") in 1942. Lehman was the state's first Jewish governor; [David Paterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Paterson "David Paterson") was the first African American governor of New York, and the first legally blind governor as well. Paterson is only the fourth African American to hold the office of governor in the United States. The current governor is [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Democratic_Committee "New York State Democratic Committee")[Kathy Hochul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathy_Hochul "Kathy Hochul"), the state's first female governor, who assumed the office on August 24, 2021, upon the resignation of [Andrew Cuomo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Cuomo "Andrew Cuomo").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-cuomo-resignation-6) Hochul went on to be elected as governor for a full term, after beating Republican Lee Zeldin in the 2022 election.

## Governors

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_governors_of_New_York&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Governors")]

For the period before independence, see [List of colonial governors of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_colonial_governors_of_New_York "List of colonial governors of New York").

New York was one of the original [Thirteen Colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteen_Colonies "Thirteen Colonies") on the east coast of North America, and was admitted as a state on July 26, 1788. Prior to declaring its independence, New York was a [colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_New_York "Province of New York") of the [Kingdom of Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Great_Britain "Kingdom of Great Britain"), which it in turn obtained from the [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") as the colony of [New Netherland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Netherland "New Netherland"); see the [list of colonial governors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_colonial_governors_of_New_York "List of colonial governors of New York") and the [list of directors-general of New Netherland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_New_Netherland "Director of New Netherland") for the pre-statehood period.

The office of the governor was established by the first [New York Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_New_York "Constitution of New York") in 1777. The governor originally served for a term of three years,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-7) though the constitution did not specify when the term began. A 1787 law set the start of the term at July 1.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-8) The [New York State Constitutional Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Constitution "New York Constitution") of 1821 amended the state constitution, reducing the term of office to two years,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-9) moving the election to November,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-10) and moving the beginning and the end of the term to coincide with the calendar year.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-11) An 1874 amendment extended the term of office back to three years,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-12) but the 1894 constitution again reduced it to two years.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-13) The most recent New York Constitution of 1938 extended the term to the current four years.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-14) There is no limit to the number of consecutive terms a governor may serve.

The Constitution has provided since 1777 for the election of a [lieutenant governor of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_Governor_of_New_York "Lieutenant Governor of New York"), who is _[ex officio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ex\_officio\_member "Ex officio member")_ President of the Senate, to the same term (keeping the same term lengths as the governor throughout all the constitutional revisions). Originally, in the event of the death, resignation or [impeachment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_in_the_United_States "Impeachment in the United States") of the governor, the lieutenant governor would become acting governor until the end of the yearly legislative term, the office being filled in a special election, if there was a remainder of the term.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-15) Since the 1821 Constitution, the lieutenant governor explicitly becomes governor upon such vacancy in the office and serves for the entire remainder of the term.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-16) Should the office of lieutenant governor become vacant, the [president _pro tempore_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_pro_tempore "President pro tempore") of the State Senate[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-17) performs all the duties of the lieutenant governor until the vacancy is filled either at the next gubernatorial election or by appointment.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-18) Likewise, should both offices become vacant at the same time, the president _pro tempore_ acts as governor, with the office of lieutenant governor remaining vacant. Should the presidency _pro tempore_ be vacant too, or the incumbent unable to fulfill the duties, the Speaker of the State Assembly is next in the line of succession.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-19) The lieutenant governor is elected on the same [ticket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ticket_(election) "Ticket (election)") as the governor, since the [1954 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_New_York_state_election "1954 New York state election") with a single joint vote cast for both offices, but is nominated separately.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-20)

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Kathy_Hochul_February_2024.jpg/250px-Kathy_Hochul_February_2024.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kathy_Hochul_February_2024.jpg)

[Kathy Hochul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathy_Hochul "Kathy Hochul") has been governor since August 24, 2021. She is the first woman to hold the position. 

The [governor of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_New_York "Governor of New York") is the [head of government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_government "Head of government") of the [U.S. state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State "New York State"), the head of the [executive branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_(government) "Executive (government)") of [New York's state government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_New_York_(state) "Government of New York (state)"), and the [commander-in-chief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander-in-chief "Commander-in-chief") of the state's [military forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Division_of_Military_and_Naval_Affairs "New York State Division of Military and Naval Affairs").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-a4s3-1) The officeholder has a duty to enforce state laws, to convene the [New York State Legislature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Legislature "New York State Legislature"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-a4s3-1) the power to either approve or [veto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veto "Veto")[bills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_(law) "Bill (law)") passed by the legislature,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-2) as well as to grant [pardons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pardon "Pardon"), except in cases of [treason](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treason "Treason") and [impeachment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_in_the_United_States "Impeachment in the United States").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-3)

Fifty-seven people have served as state governor, four of whom served non-consecutive terms ([George Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Clinton_(vice_president) "George Clinton (vice president)"), [DeWitt Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeWitt_Clinton "DeWitt Clinton"), [Horatio Seymour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horatio_Seymour "Horatio Seymour"), and [Al Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Smith "Al Smith")); the official numbering lists each governor only once. There has only been one female governor so far: [Kathy Hochul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathy_Hochul "Kathy Hochul"). This numbering includes one acting governor: the lieutenant governor who filled the vacancy after the resignation of the governor, under the 1777 Constitution.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-4) The list does not include the prior colonial governors nor those who have acted as governor when the governor was out of state, such as Lieutenant Governor Timothy L. Woodruff during Theodore Roosevelt's vice presidential campaign in 1900, or Acting [Speaker of the New York State Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Speakers_of_the_New_York_State_Assembly "List of Speakers of the New York State Assembly")[Moses M. Weinstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_M._Weinstein "Moses M. Weinstein"), who acted as governor for 10 days in 1968 while the governor, the Lieutenant Governor and the Senate Majority Leader were out of the state, attending the Republican National Convention in [Miami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami "Miami").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-5)

Four men have become [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") after serving as governor of New York: [Martin Van Buren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Van_Buren "Martin Van Buren"), [Grover Cleveland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grover_Cleveland "Grover Cleveland"), [Theodore Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Roosevelt "Theodore Roosevelt"), and [Franklin D. Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt "Franklin D. Roosevelt"), and six were [vice president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_president_of_the_United_States "Vice president of the United States"). Van Buren and Theodore Roosevelt held both offices. Numerous Governors have also sought the Presidency, and won their party's respective nomination, but lost the general election, such as [Al Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Smith "Al Smith"), [Samuel J. Tilden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_J._Tilden "Samuel J. Tilden"), [Horatio Seymour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horatio_Seymour "Horatio Seymour"), [Thomas E. Dewey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_E._Dewey "Thomas E. Dewey"), and [Charles Evans Hughes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Evans_Hughes "Charles Evans Hughes"). Two governors have been [chief justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_Justice_of_the_United_States "Chief Justice of the United States"): [John Jay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Jay "John Jay") held that position when he was elected governor in 1795, and [Charles Evans Hughes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Evans_Hughes "Charles Evans Hughes") became chief justice in 1930, two decades after leaving the governorship.

The longest-serving governor was the first, [George Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Clinton_(vice_president) "George Clinton (vice president)"), who first took office on July 30, 1777, and served seven terms in two different periods, totaling just under 21 years in office. As 18 of those years were consecutive, Clinton also served the longest consecutive period in office for a New York governor. [Charles Poletti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Poletti "Charles Poletti") had the shortest term, serving 29 days following the resignation of the previous governor, [Herbert H. Lehman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbert_H._Lehman "Herbert H. Lehman") in 1942. Lehman was the state's first Jewish governor; [David Paterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Paterson "David Paterson") was the first African American governor of New York, and the first legally blind governor as well. Paterson is only the fourth African American to hold the office of governor in the United States. The current governor is [Democrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Democratic_Committee "New York State Democratic Committee")[Kathy Hochul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathy_Hochul "Kathy Hochul"), the state's first female governor, who assumed the office on August 24, 2021, upon the resignation of [Andrew Cuomo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Cuomo "Andrew Cuomo").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-cuomo-resignation-6) Hochul went on to be elected as governor for a full term, after beating Republican Lee Zeldin in the 2022 election.

## Governors

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_governors_of_New_York&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Governors")]

For the period before independence, see [List of colonial governors of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_colonial_governors_of_New_York "List of colonial governors of New York").

New York was one of the original [Thirteen Colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thirteen_Colonies "Thirteen Colonies") on the east coast of North America, and was admitted as a state on July 26, 1788. Prior to declaring its independence, New York was a [colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_New_York "Province of New York") of the [Kingdom of Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Great_Britain "Kingdom of Great Britain"), which it in turn obtained from the [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands") as the colony of [New Netherland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Netherland "New Netherland"); see the [list of colonial governors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_colonial_governors_of_New_York "List of colonial governors of New York") and the [list of directors-general of New Netherland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_New_Netherland "Director of New Netherland") for the pre-statehood period.

The office of the governor was established by the first [New York Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_New_York "Constitution of New York") in 1777. The governor originally served for a term of three years,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-7) though the constitution did not specify when the term began. A 1787 law set the start of the term at July 1.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-8) The [New York State Constitutional Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Constitution "New York Constitution") of 1821 amended the state constitution, reducing the term of office to two years,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-9) moving the election to November,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-10) and moving the beginning and the end of the term to coincide with the calendar year.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-11) An 1874 amendment extended the term of office back to three years,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-12) but the 1894 constitution again reduced it to two years.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-13) The most recent New York Constitution of 1938 extended the term to the current four years.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-14) There is no limit to the number of consecutive terms a governor may serve.

The Constitution has provided since 1777 for the election of a [lieutenant governor of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lieutenant_Governor_of_New_York "Lieutenant Governor of New York"), who is _[ex officio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ex\_officio\_member "Ex officio member")_ President of the Senate, to the same term (keeping the same term lengths as the governor throughout all the constitutional revisions). Originally, in the event of the death, resignation or [impeachment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impeachment_in_the_United_States "Impeachment in the United States") of the governor, the lieutenant governor would become acting governor until the end of the yearly legislative term, the office being filled in a special election, if there was a remainder of the term.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-15) Since the 1821 Constitution, the lieutenant governor explicitly becomes governor upon such vacancy in the office and serves for the entire remainder of the term.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-16) Should the office of lieutenant governor become vacant, the [president _pro tempore_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_pro_tempore "President pro tempore") of the State Senate[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-17) performs all the duties of the lieutenant governor until the vacancy is filled either at the next gubernatorial election or by appointment.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-18) Likewise, should both offices become vacant at the same time, the president _pro tempore_ acts as governor, with the office of lieutenant governor remaining vacant. Should the presidency _pro tempore_ be vacant too, or the incumbent unable to fulfill the duties, the Speaker of the State Assembly is next in the line of succession.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-19) The lieutenant governor is elected on the same [ticket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ticket_(election) "Ticket (election)") as the governor, since the [1954 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1954_New_York_state_election "1954 New York state election") with a single joint vote cast for both offices, but is nominated separately.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governors_of_New_York#cite_note-20)
